formalization.project_name: The Baire product theorem for Choquet spaces

mathematical_sources.note: Printed p.2 explicitly recalls that a Baire space times a Banach–Mazur alpha-favorable space is Baire, citing H.E.White1975. Section2, printed pp.2–3, specifies full finite opponent-history strategies and common-point payoffs. The proof here develops a disjoint dense rectangle tree and coherent branch, not a claimed reproduction of the original White proof, which was not consulted. The strong-Choquet beta-unfavorability Theorem1.1, almost-locally-ccc products and Krom theorems are outside scope. No novelty, priority or first-formalization claim.
mathematical_sources.title: More on products of Baire spaces, arXiv:1702.06197v3

related_formalizations.note: Canonical topology, BaireSpace, dense/Gδ sets, Zorn, metric and filter completeness provide infrastructure. Exact material imported definitions and proof dependencies retain pinned source excerpts and independently compiled semantic bridges. No matching Choquet strategy or arbitrary Baire-times-alpha-favorable product theorem was located in this exact revision.

Two maximal-disjoint/dense-refinement helpers are reused under Apache-2.0 with attribution. The rectangle-tree architecture is adapted from this prior compact-fiber argument; the new full-history strategy branch replaces compact-fiber intersection. No cross-project import or locally compact assumption is used. The game-history convention also credits Banach–Mazur source59d4a50df466480e88ab71bc1f3527bfe0bf1811.
